result: Compilation succeeded. I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtilsAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering `DateUtils`'s documented contract: the millisecond constants, all `addXxx`/`setXxx` methods (including boundary/invalid-range cases), `ceiling`/`round`/`truncate` (Date/Calendar/Object overloads, DST-free examples from the javadoc, `ArithmeticException` on year overflow, `ClassCastException` on bad `Object` input), the `getFragmentInXxx` family using the exact documented examples, `isSameDay`/`isSameInstant`/`isSameLocalTime`, the `iterator` overloads (range styles, invalid range style, type dispatch), `parseDate`/`parseDateStrictly` (locale handling, strict vs. lenient overflow, whole-string matching, `ParseException`/`NullPointerException` cases), `toCalendar`, `toLocalDateTime`/`toOffsetDateTime`/`toZonedDateTime`, and `truncatedCompareTo`/`truncatedEquals`. All syntax is Java 8-compatible (anonymous `Executable` classes instead of lambdas, no diamond operator, no underscored literals), and `./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
